Statement 1: If Gaussian elimination works, then LU decomposition can also be used.
- Gaussian elimination without pivoting works when no zero pivots are encountered. LU decomposition (without pivoting) requires the same conditions. However, Gaussian elimination is more commonly associated with partial pivoting for stability. But generally, if Gaussian elimination can be performed (with or without pivoting), LU decomposition can also be performed. Actually, standard LU decomposition (without pivoting) has the same stability requirements as Gaussian elimination without pivoting. If we include pivoting (LU with partial pivoting), then Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting works in more cases. So the statement depends on what we mean by "works." If we mean "can be successfully applied to solve the system," both can solve any non-singular system if pivoting is used. If we mean "can be applied without pivoting," then both have the same restrictions. Either way, this statement is generally considered correct.

Statement 2: If LU decomposition works, then Gaussian elimination can also be used.
- Gaussian elimination and LU decomposition are essentially the same algorithm. If LU decomposition works (i.e., the matrix can be decomposed into L and U), then Gaussian elimination can also solve the system. This is correct.

Statement 3: If Gauss-Seidel works, then TDMA can also be used.
- Gauss-Seidel is an iterative method that works for diagonally dominant or symmetric positive definite matrices. TDMA (Tridiagonal Matrix Algorithm) is a direct method for tridiagonal systems. The key question is: does "Gauss-Seidel works" imply "TDMA works"? Gauss-Seidel works on a broad class of matrices, including diagonally dominant ones. But TDMA specifically requires the matrix to be tridiagonal. If the matrix is not tridiagonal, TDMA cannot be used directly. So Gauss-Seidel might work on a matrix that is not tridiagonal, where TDMA doesn't apply. But if Gauss-Seidel works on a tridiagonal system, then TDMA can also be used. However, the statement says "If Gauss-Seidel works, then TDMA can also be used" - this implies that whenever Gauss-Seidel is applicable, TDMA is also applicable. Since Gauss-Seidel can work on non-tridiagonal matrices, this statement is incorrect in general.
